title: Android HAL
description: Treble, HIDL vs. AIDL HALs, VINTF, Binder domains, versioning and debugging.

questions.question: Which Android version introduced Project Treble?
questions.explanation: Treble separated the vendor implementation from the Android framework via stable HAL interfaces.

questions.question: What is used for new HAL interfaces since Android 11?
questions.explanation: HIDL is deprecated for new HALs; existing HIDL HALs are being migrated to AIDL.

questions.question: Which statements about stable AIDL HALs are correct?

answers.text: The interface is declared with an aidl_interface module and stability "vintf"
Released versions are frozen; their API dumps live in aidl_api/
You may change method signatures in a frozen version

questions.explanation: Changes go into a new version; you can add methods at the end and new fields to parcelables.

questions.question: What do the VINTF device manifest and framework compatibility matrix describe?

answers.text: Which HALs the device provides and which HALs the framework requires

questions.explanation: They are checked at build time and OTA time to ensure system and vendor images match.

questions.question: Which service managers are used?
questions.explanation: They correspond to /dev/binder, /dev/hwbinder and /dev/vndbinder.

questions.question: What is the difference between binderized and passthrough HIDL HALs?

answers.text: Binderized: own process, IPC via hwbinder; passthrough: loaded into the client process

questions.explanation: Passthrough mode was mainly a migration path for legacy HALs.

questions.question: How were legacy (pre-Treble) HALs loaded?

answers.text: hw_get_module() loads a shared library, e.g. from /vendor/lib/hw, exposing hw_module_t

questions.explanation: Legacy HALs are C structs with function pointers in a .so.

questions.question: Which AIDL backends exist?
questions.explanation: There is also the C++ libbinder backend. For vendor HALs, the NDK backend is recommended.

questions.question: What do you need to add for a new HAL service besides the code?

answers.text: An init .rc file to start the service

questions.explanation: Without SELinux policy and manifest entry, registration fails or the framework can't find the HAL.

questions.question: What does a 'oneway' AIDL method mean?

answers.text: The call returns immediately without waiting for the result
The method can only be called once
Only one client may call it

questions.explanation: oneway calls can't return values; they are queued per Binder object.

questions.question: How can a client react when a HAL process dies?

answers.text: Register a death recipient via linkToDeath()

questions.explanation: After the death notification, the client re-fetches the service when it's back.

questions.question: What are lazy HALs?

answers.text: HALs that start on demand and can exit when no clients are connected

questions.explanation: They save memory; AIDL lazy services use LazyServiceRegistrar and an init service that is not started at boot.

questions.question: Which command lists registered AIDL services on a device?
questions.explanation: lshal lists HIDL HALs.

questions.question: Which partition usually contains HAL implementations?
questions.explanation: Keeping them on vendor/odm allows updating /system independently, e.g. with a GSI.

questions.question: What is a GSI (Generic System Image)?

answers.text: A pure AOSP system image that boots on Treble-compliant devices
A vendor image for all devices

questions.explanation: GSIs are used for VTS/CTS-on-GSI testing of the vendor interface.

questions.question: How do you freeze a new version of an AIDL interface in AOSP?

answers.text: Increase the version in Android.bp manually

questions.explanation: This creates the next aidl_api/<name>/<version> dump; 'm <name>-update-api' updates the current dump.

questions.question: A client built against version 1 talks to a version 2 HAL. What applies?

answers.text: The client can check the remote version via getInterfaceVersion()

questions.explanation: Calling a method the remote doesn't implement returns UNKNOWN_TRANSACTION, so check the version first.

questions.question: Which test suite verifies that a vendor implementation follows the HAL interfaces?
questions.explanation: VTS tests HAL implementations and the kernel; CTS tests the app-facing API.

questions.question: Why are HAL interfaces versioned and frozen?

answers.text: So that framework and vendor images can be updated independently

questions.explanation: This is the core idea of Treble: a stable interface between framework and vendor.

questions.question: What is the descriptor of an AIDL HAL instance typically like?
questions.explanation: The same name is listed in the VINTF manifest and used with AServiceManager_waitForService().
